title: Deus Irae
theological_headline: PKD names Deus Irae as the religious source-stream of VALIS — one theme fused into his final vision of God.
intro:
*Deus Irae*, PKD's post-nuclear theodicy of the God of Wrath, appears once in the Exegesis — not as a reading of its pilgrimage or its rival deities, but as one of the three named tributaries he says flowed into *VALIS*. It supplies, in his own accounting, the "religious theme." (Lane B: PKD reading his own corpus.)

The single mention is structural rather than interpretive, so this page keeps to that use: how *Deus Irae* functions in PKD's story of how his novels fused into one vision.
theological_synthesis:
The theological use is genealogical. In [89:105] PKD reports a "stoned insight" that 2-3-74 was the flash in which the independent regions of his thinking — politics, religion, metaphysics, his actual life, history — fused into "one great new synthesis" subsumed beneath a vision of God. Within that account *VALIS* is "a fusion of the political theme of *Tears*, the religious theme of *Deus Irae*, and the street patois and split personality and dope themes of *Scanner*."

*Deus Irae* is thus assigned a single load-bearing role: it is where the religious material of his corpus was carried, later absorbed into *VALIS*. The passage does not analyze the God of Wrath against the Christian God or the pilgrimage to depict God; it names the novel to show that PKD's mature theology did not arrive from nowhere but fused strands he had already worked out separately — the religious strand being *Deus Irae*'s.

mentions.summary: Stoned insight: I assimilated my theology, metaphysics, epistemology and philosophy to my political beliefs. _They_ are all changed but the political beliefs remain the same; they ratify my political beliefs. They give it cosmic timeless scope; it is validated by and issues from divine authority. _VALIS_ is a fusion of the political theme of _Tears,_ the religious theme of _Deus Irae,_ and the street patois and split personality and dope themes of _Scanner_ —it logically follows the three previous novels. **** and other aspects: death and loss, friends. So I _am_ right; 2-3-74 represented a flash in which the independent areas of my thinking fused into one great _new_ synthesis in which everything I had thought before was subsumed beneath a vision of God. [...] _VALIS_ is composed of: (1) My 10 volume meta-novel (2) Politics (3) Religion (4) My actual life (5) History all fused together into a total vision that is a structure emanating out of the mutual exchange of (between, among) these five elements up to then existing independent of one another in my mind.
quotes: _VALIS_ is a fusion of the political theme of _Tears,_ the religious theme of _Deus Irae,_ and the street patois and split personality and dope themes of _Scanner_ —it logically follows the three previous novels.
mentions.gloss: PKD names *Deus Irae* as the "religious theme" fused into *VALIS*, alongside the political theme of *Tears* and the dope-and-split-self themes of *Scanner*. In his account of 2-3-74 as the flash that merged politics, religion, life, and history into one vision of God, *Deus Irae* is the religious tributary — cited for its role in the synthesis, not read here for its God of Wrath or its pilgrimage.
